headline: A small South Korean maker of X-ray inspection machines has started supplying tools that check AI memory chips to Micron and hopes for Samsung and SK hynix orders from 2027.
score_reason: Niche supplier story built on analyst projections; kept at the pool level.
importance_line: Better inspection of stacked AI memory could help makers raise yields, which touches memory makers and their equipment suppliers, but the Samsung and SK hynix orders are only hoped-for and the supplier is still loss-making.
source: BigGo Finance, citing Researchalum and NH Investment & Securities
summary: BigGo Finance reports, citing analysts at Researchalum and NH Investment & Securities, that South Korea's SEC Co. sold eight manual X-ray inspection systems for high-bandwidth memory (HBM, the fast stacked memory used with AI chips) to Micron in 2025 and is testing production-line versions with Samsung Electronics and SK hynix. Orders could come as early as the first quarter of 2027 if it passes quality tests; the company posted a first-half operating loss of 7.7 billion won.
notes: Credit chain unclear: BigGo is an aggregator; written as "BigGo reports, citing" the named analysts.
